sources.title: The Comics History of the Morlocks

events.documented_observation: Storm defeats Callisto in a knife duel to stop the Morlocks holding Angel and assumes leadership.
Callisto finds Caliban and uses his mutant-detection ability to locate other outcasts and establish the underground community.
Caliban attempts to abduct Kitty at a Dazzler concert; Storm and Jessica Drew intervene.
After Kitty agrees to marriage in exchange for help saving Colossus, Caliban releases her when he realizes she does not love him.

events.scope: Morlock childhood to Gene Nation period, before Uncanny X-Men #325 (1995)
events.documented_observation: Marvel’s Marrow biography says Callisto raised Sarah in the tunnels and trained her.

events.scope: Mutant Massacre (1986), later revealed in Uncanny X-Men #350-era backstory
events.documented_observation: Marvel’s Marrow biography says Gambit rescued young Sarah during the Marauders’ attack, despite his role in bringing the killers into the tunnels.
Marrow connects explosives on civilian hostages to her own heartbeat and challenges Storm; Storm stops her heart to prevent detonation.

events.scope: X-Men late 1990s, after Operation: Zero Tolerance (1997)
events.documented_observation: Marvel’s biography describes Wolverine taking responsibility for trying to rehabilitate Marrow, with repeated arguments and fights.

events.scope: Pre-Mutant Massacre Morlock period, before X-Factor #9 (1986)
events.documented_observation: Annalee cares for young Leech after losing her biological children; Marvel lists Leech as an adopted son.
Marvel states that Scalphunter kills Annalee during the Marauders’ slaughter of Morlocks.
Lucia and Maria are sisters; Marvel describes Thornn opposing Feral after Maria joins X-Force and Lucia the Brotherhood.
The publisher synopsis explicitly says Skids, Rusty and Mirage work to protect Artie, Leech and babies.

events.scope: Fantastic Four (1998) #579 and Future Foundation era (2010 onward)
events.documented_observation: Marvel identifies Leech as Artie Maddicks’ friend and recruits them into the Future Foundation.
Skids helps Rusty evade Freedom Force; Marvel’s Julia Carpenter history identifies Skids among those who helped Rusty escape.
Carl attempts to cure Artie’s mutation, then stays behind to distract armed security so Artie, Beast and X-Factor can escape; he dies.
Carl has Beast kidnapped and subjects him to experimental mutation-reversal treatment without his consent.

claims.documented_fact: Callisto duels Storm over leadership and the captive Angel.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: A specific contest for leadership, not proof of permanent personal hatred.

claims.documented_fact: Storm defeats Callisto and assumes leadership of the Morlocks.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: Leadership acquired by duel; no evidence that all Morlocks embraced her decisions.

claims.documented_fact: Callisto uses Caliban’s ability to locate other mutants for the community.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: A directed recruitment/use of his skill; his feelings about this arrangement are not established.
Loneliness does not negate the attempted abduction or establish mutual romance.

claims.documented_fact: Caliban releases Kitty from the marriage vow when he learns she does not love him.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: Unreciprocated attachment; his later restraint does not validate the earlier kidnapping.

claims.documented_fact: Callisto raises and trains Sarah in the Morlock tunnels.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: Guardian-like training is publisher-biography evidence; legal adoption is not established.

claims.documented_fact: Gambit rescues Sarah during the massacre.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: One rescue does not erase his complicity in bringing the Marauders to the tunnels.

claims.documented_fact: Marrow forces a confrontation with Storm using civilians as leverage.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: Marrow’s stated grievance is historically situated; it is not a permanent assessment of Storm.

claims.documented_fact: Wolverine attempts to rehabilitate and guide Marrow.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: The biography describes mixed results and fights; no enduring mutual trust inferred.

claims.documented_fact: Marvel lists Leech as Annalee’s adopted son and describes her caring for him.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: Publisher page is explicitly unverified; adoption’s legal status not panel-confirmed.

claims.documented_fact: Scalphunter kills Annalee during the Mutant Massacre.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: No prior personal vendetta is established; exact killing panel not independently reviewed.
Kinship remains despite their 1990s opposing allegiances.
Reciprocal kinship, not evidence of mutual affection in the conflict.

claims.documented_fact: Skids helps protect Artie in New Mutants #73.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: A concrete group protection action, not indefinite guardianship.

claims.documented_fact: Marvel explicitly identifies Leech as Artie’s friend.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: Friendship directly stated; no claims about private motivations.

claims.documented_fact: Skids helps Rusty evade Freedom Force.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: Incident-specific assistance; romance not inferred from rescue.

claims.documented_fact: Carl sacrifices his chance to escape to protect Artie from security forces.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: Protective final act coexists with Carl’s earlier nonconsensual plan to alter Artie’s body.

claims.documented_fact: Carl kidnaps Beast and experiments on him without consent.
claims.interpretation_or_limit: His stated desire to cure Artie does not make the treatment consensual.

research_limits: Marvel character biographies for Marrow, Annalee and Thornn explicitly say crowd-sourced content is unverified.
Original issue panels not examined; issue-level synopses are publisher summaries, not panel review.
Leech friendship and Skids protection are supported by Marvel editorial/issue summaries; do not infer permanent loyalty.
